name: Scale-up allowance
amount:
allowance.amount
* (period.part == period.parts
  ? ((employment.start_date <= period.month_from
  && (employment.exit_date == ""
  ||employment.exit_date >= period.month_to))
    ?1.0
    :double(
      calendar_distance_days(
        employment.start_date > period.month_from
          ?employment.start_date
          :period.month_from,
        (employment.exit_date != ""
        &&employment.exit_date < period.month_to)
          ?employment.exit_date
          :period.month_to
      )
      +1.0
    )
    /double(period.month_days))
  - (allowance.amount > 0.0
    ? (has(earned.month.SUA) ? earned.month.SUA : 0.0)
    / (allowance.amount)
    :0.0)
  : ((employment.start_date <= period.month_from
  && (employment.exit_date == ""
  ||employment.exit_date >= period.month_to))
    ?1.0 / double(period.parts)
    :double(period.paid_days) / double(period.month_days)))

name: Child care allowance (children aged 12 and under)

references.title: LHDN Specification for MTD Calculations Using Computerised Calculation 2026 (https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-2026.pdf), E(9), pp.20–22, read 28 September 2026 item ii: child care allowance for children up to 12 years of age, received by the employee or paid directly to the child care centre, is exempt up to RM3,000 a year (raised from the RM2,400 of LHDN Public Ruling 5/2019 Perquisites from Employment (https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/PR_05_2019_2.pdf) para 7.2.4). PCB.assessed_on and PCB.ordinary_on subtract annual_exempt(…, 3,000); the rest is normal remuneration. EPF Act 1991 s.2 “wages” (AGC text as at 1 July 2022) includes any bonus, commission or allowance and excludes any travelling allowance; KWSP employer FAQ (Mandatory Contribution, Q8 “Components of Wage”: salary, bonus, allowance, commission, incentives; Q11 “Non-Wages”: travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession; read 28 September 2026 in the browser): an allowance is EPF wages. Act 4 s.2(24) and Act 800 s.2 include any allowance paid in money and exclude none of this kind: SOCSO, EIS and SKBBK wages. Act 612 s.2 “wages” (AGC reprint 2017): basic salary and fixed allowances or other emoluments of a like nature paid in cash, excluding (b) any travelling allowance, (c) special expenses and (e) any bonus or commission: a fixed cash allowance is HRD wages. Employment Act 1955 s.2 “wages” (AGC reprint as at 1 August 2023): basic wages and all other payments in cash payable for work done under the contract, excluding (c) any travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession: a cash payment under the contract, so wages. The RM3,000 limit has applied since YA2024 (Income Tax (Exemption) (Amendment) Order 2023, P.U.(A) 399/2023, raising the RM2,400), so every version from December 2025 carries it. Sub-monthly settlement (2026-10-08): a fixed allowance is monthly wages under EA s.18A — the whole month ÷ the parts, a part month the employed days ÷ the month's calendar days, the last part settling the month less what the earlier parts paid.

name: Meal allowance (regular, same rate for all)

references.title: LHDN Specification for MTD Calculations Using Computerised Calculation 2026 (https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-2026.pdf), E(9), pp.20–22, read 28 September 2026 item vii and LHDN Public Ruling 5/2019 Perquisites from Employment (https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/PR_05_2019_2.pdf) para 7.2.3 (p.22, Example 19: RM250 a month exempt): a meal allowance received on a regular basis at the same rate to all employees is exempt from tax, so this class counts toward no PCB base. EPF Act 1991 s.2 “wages” (AGC text as at 1 July 2022) includes any bonus, commission or allowance and excludes any travelling allowance; KWSP employer FAQ (Mandatory Contribution, Q8 “Components of Wage”: salary, bonus, allowance, commission, incentives; Q11 “Non-Wages”: travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession; read 28 September 2026 in the browser): an allowance is EPF wages. Act 4 s.2(24) and Act 800 s.2 include any allowance paid in money; a cash meal allowance is not a special expense of the employment: SOCSO, EIS and SKBBK wages. Act 612 s.2 “wages” (AGC reprint 2017): basic salary and fixed allowances or other emoluments of a like nature paid in cash, excluding (b) any travelling allowance, (c) special expenses and (e) any bonus or commission: a fixed cash allowance is HRD wages. Employment Act 1955 s.2 “wages” (AGC reprint as at 1 August 2023): basic wages and all other payments in cash payable for work done under the contract, excluding (c) any travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession: a cash payment, not the in-kind “supply of any food” of exclusion (a), so wages. Owner rule 2026-09-28: the law is silent on a regular meal allowance under Act 4 s.2(24)(c); default — not a special expense (it does not arise from the nature of the work), so wages; lawful because it charges the contribution. An overtime or outstation meal allowance at an internal-circular rate is not this class. Sub-monthly settlement (2026-10-08): a fixed allowance is monthly wages under EA s.18A — the whole month ÷ the parts, a part month the employed days ÷ the month's calendar days, the last part settling the month less what the earlier parts paid.

name: Parking allowance

references.title: LHDN Specification for MTD Calculations Using Computerised Calculation 2026 (https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-2026.pdf), E(9), pp.20–22, read 28 September 2026 item vi and LHDN Public Ruling 5/2019 Perquisites from Employment (https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/PR_05_2019_2.pdf) para 7.2.2 (pp.21–22, Example 18: RM180 a month exempt): a parking rate or parking allowance, including a rate paid by the employer directly to the operator, is exempt from tax, so this class counts toward no PCB base. EPF Act 1991 s.2 “wages” (AGC text as at 1 July 2022) includes any bonus, commission or allowance and excludes any travelling allowance; KWSP employer FAQ (Mandatory Contribution, Q8 “Components of Wage”: salary, bonus, allowance, commission, incentives; Q11 “Non-Wages”: travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession; read 28 September 2026 in the browser): an allowance is EPF wages. name: Piece-rate pay

references.title: EA ss.60(3)(d), 60A(3)(a), 60D(3)(a)(ii), (aaa): a piece-rated employee is paid the rate per piece (roster day facts piece_units, piece_rate, else terms.base_salary), twice it on a rest day or a paid holiday, 1.5 times it for overtime pieces (overtime_units) and three times on a holiday. EA First Schedule paras 1A–2: these premia bind an employee earning not more than RM4,000 a month (s.2 wages less commission, subsistence and overtime: terms.monthly_wage) or engaged in manual labour, supervising it, operating or maintaining a commercial vehicle, or as vessel crew, whatever the pay; not a domestic employee (para 2(5)); terms.facts.overtime_by_contract applies them by contract. Rest day (2026-10-08, confirmation B3): EA s.60(3)(d) pays a piece-rated employee working on a rest day "twice his ordinary rate per piece" — every piece of the day, its overtime pieces included, at 2× (1.5× overtime pieces only on a working day; 3× on a holiday).

amount:
(1.0)
* (sum(
  work.days.filter(d, has(d.facts) && has(d.facts.piece_units)).map(
    d,
    double(d.facts.piece_units)
    * (has(d.facts.piece_rate)
      ?double(d.facts.piece_rate)
      :terms.base_salary)
    * (d.holiday_kind
    in ["PUBLIC_HOLIDAY", "SUBSTITUTE", "DOUBLE_HOLIDAY"]
    ||d.day_type == "REST"
      ?2.0
      :1.0)
    + (has(d.facts.overtime_units)
      ?double(d.facts.overtime_units)
      * (has(d.facts.piece_rate)
        ?double(d.facts.piece_rate)
        :terms.base_salary)
      * (d.holiday_kind
      in ["PUBLIC_HOLIDAY", "SUBSTITUTE", "DOUBLE_HOLIDAY"]
        ?3.0
        :d.day_type == "REST" ? 2.0 : 1.5)
      :0.0
  ) )
))
